intro: Granada rewards slow walkers with palaces, tea houses, and Alhambra views at sunset, plus tapas bars along steep, winding lanes. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: One metro line runs in Granada. A single ticket costs about €1.65 (Nov 2024). A rechargeable green travel card costs €1.50 at tobacco shops and needs at least €5 of credit.
Local buses cover most sights. Alhambra Buses (C30 to the Alhambra, C31 to Albayzin, C34 to Sacromonte) cost €1.60 per trip (Nov 2024). Multi-trip cards cost €5, €10 or €20.
Taxis are easy to find. Ride apps such as Uber or Cabify: check locally.
Driving in the centre is restricted. Camera-enforced limits apply, so park outside the historic core or use a garage such as Parking HH Maristas.
Walking is the best way to see the old quarters, but streets are steep, narrow and uneven. Buses help on the hills.
No ferry service applies to Granada.

royal_chapel.name: Royal Chapel of Granada

old_town.name: Granada Old Town

alhambra_night.name: Alhambra night visit

alhambra_night.hours: Evenings in season; check on the day
alhambra_night.tip: Choose a night ticket for a quieter, lit-up visit, and bring a light jacket.

generalife_gardens.name: Generalife gardens
generalife_gardens.hours: Same as Generalife; check on the day
generalife_gardens.tip: Walk the long pool and cypress paths for the quietest part of the complex.

cathedral_roof.name: Cathedral roof and tower visit
cathedral_roof.price_text: Included in cathedral ticket or extra; check on the day

albayzin_sunset.name: Albayzín sunset walk

albayzin_sunset.hours: Best 1 hour before sunset; check on the day

royal_chapel_tombs.name: Royal tombs and museum

royal_chapel_tombs.tip: Look at the Gothic tombs first, then the museum rooms with paintings and royal objects.

sacromonte_flamenco.name: Sacromonte flamenco show

sacromonte_flamenco.hours: Evening shows, usually one or two sittings; check on the day
sacromonte_flamenco.tip: Book a cave venue in advance and ask whether drinks are included.

san_agustin_market.name: San Agustín food market

san_agustin_market.hours: Typically weekday daytime; check on the day
san_agustin_market.tip: Sample local produce and tapas, and ask vendors what is in season.

hammam.name: Hammam Al Ándalus baths
hammam.price_text: Approx. €25–40 per session; check current price
hammam.hours: Daily sessions; booking required; check on the day

mirador_san_nicolas.name: Mirador de San Nicolás

darro_walk.name: Carrera del Darro riverside walk

stays.why: Central base near Plaza Nueva and the Cathedral. Easy walks, many restaurants, but busy and noisy at night.
Historic hillside quarter facing the Alhambra. Great views and romantic streets, but steep and uneven. Bring comfortable shoes.
Calm former Jewish quarter with local bars and a relaxed feel. Quieter than Centro and close to the historic core.
Cave-house neighbourhood known for flamenco. Atmospheric, but far from the centre and best reached by bus or taxi at night.

food: Tapas often come free with a drink in many bars. Order a drink and ask what comes with it; check on the day.
Try the local dish of habas con jamón (broad beans with ham) and piononos, a small rolled sponge cake.
Eat early or book ahead for dinner. Many kitchens open around 20:00 to 21:00 and fill quickly in high season.
Visit a covered market such as Mercado San Agustín for fresh produce and cheap snacks.
Plan a tapas crawl in Centro or Realejo, where bars are close together and walkable.
more_time: Mountain fans: take a day trip to the Sierra Nevada. Check bus times and snow conditions before you go.
Villages and walks: visit the white villages of the Alpujarras by bus or tour. Check services, as they run less often.
Wider day trip: visit Córdoba or Sevilla for more Moorish and Andalusian history. Check train or coach times in advance.
